A stdio agent's lifetime belongs to the framework

Features·seedling·accepted·JUL 16, 2026

serveOverStdio reports link death as a value and leaves process exit to every app — so a forgotten exit (or any live timer) yields an immortal orphan agent. Bind process lifetime to the link at the construction that means "this process IS the agent," making the orphan unspellable.

Contents

  • The defect class, observed in the field
  • The principle violations (why this is the framework’s bug)

The defect class, observed in the field

A fleet host (sincereintent) hit its swap alert carrying ten orphaned drishti-agent --stdio processes — 130–200 MB each, up to 23 hours old, every one re-parented to pid 1 — accumulating one per server⇄host reconnect (drishti#109). The same class litters CI boxes as T/odu/kolu/* leaves: odu’s remote lane agents are stdio-served processes too.Distinct from the SIGKILL-teardown leaf leak the flaky tracker records (no signal window at all — kolu#1851 closed the graceful half). This class is the graceful case gone wrong: the link ends cleanly, EOF is delivered, and the process still lives forever.

The mechanism is not a missing feature — the framework already documents the right intent. frontDaemonOverStdio’s header calls serveOverStdio “the ephemeral remote agent: the --stdio process is the server … when the link drops the server (and any state it held) is gone — exactly right for a re-run-fresh agent (mini-ci, remote-process-monitor, drishti).” But the implementation hands that promise to the app: serveOverStdio resolves with {reason: "end" | "error"} when the read stream ends, and process termination is the caller’s homework. Any live handle — drishti-agent’s 2s poll interval, a watcher, a child — keeps Node’s event loop alive after main returns, so the failure mode of forgetting (or sequencing cleanup wrong) is an invisible immortal orphan on someone else’s machine.

The principle violations (why this is the framework’s bug)

  • P5 — guarantee at the knowing endpoint. “This process’s reason to exist is gone” is known at exactly one place: the serve loop that saw EOF on the default stdio. The app’s main cannot reliably make the exit guarantee — it doesn’t know what else holds the event loop (that is the whole reason the orphans are invisible). The layer that knows must own the exit.
  • P4 — illegal states unrepresentable. “Agent process alive, link dead” is a constructible state today, guarded only by every app’s discipline. The perfection-review question — would the defect class become inexpressible? — says: bind lifetime structurally, don’t document it.
  • Fail-fast doctrine. Lingering after link death is a silent degradation; and the fix must not add an opt-out knob — “being able to override is never a feature.” The two lifetimes (ephemeral vs durable) are selected by construction, not configuration: that split already exists in the package family (serveOverStdio vs frontDaemonOverStdio + a socket daemon), which is what makes this fix small.

The change (one seam, discriminated by construction)

serveOverStdio already has the discriminant in hand: whether the caller passed a transport override.

  • Default transport (process.stdin/stdout) — the process IS the agent. On read-end/error (the write-EPIPE funnel already routes here): run the handler’s disposers, then process.exit(reason === "end" ? 0 : 1) — framework-owned, no knob. An optional onEnd last-gasp hook runs under a hard deadline (a wedged cleanup must not resurrect the orphan class the exit exists to kill).
  • Explicit transport override — a loopback/test/embedded peer. Current behavior stands: resolve the value, caller owns lifetime. Tests keep passing untouched; exotic compositions choose this arm by construction.

The returned promise still settles (same shape) before exit on the default arm, so a caller that today does post-settle logging keeps working — it just can no longer forget to die.

Consumers and rollout

consumer today after
drishti-agent never exits after settle → the drishti#109 orphans deletes any hand-rolled exit; inherits via the pair PR
mini-ci, remote-process-monitor named serveOverStdio users — audit for post-settle work (expected none) no change needed
odu lane agents leaves accumulate on CI boxes (T/odu/kolu/*) inherits at the next kolu pin bump — an adoption-opportunity line for the odu#43 ledger
padi unaffected — the durable arm (frontDaemonOverStdio + socket daemon); its front already dies with the relay —

Pin (red-before/green-after): serve a router over a real child-process stdio pair holding a live setInterval; kill the parent side; assert the child exits within the deadline (red today: it lives forever). Plus the override-arm pin: same scenario with an explicit transport resolves the value and does NOT exit.

Gates: framework change in @kolu/surface → the standard treatment — lens run before GO, drishti pair PR (which also closes drishti#109’s app side), ODU-IMPACT verdict (expected adoption-opportunity, ledgered), ref-surface.mdx update in the same PR.
